messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: 2026-03-15T03:14:05Z - High crashloop rate detected in prod-us-east/gpu-pool-3 (runtime-engine). SIGSEGV observed in container runtime (rate ~120/hr). Auto-created incident #INC-2026-0913.

mira: I'm taking pager for runtime. jumping in.

dan: oncall here. what's scope + customer impact?

mira: affected ~4 nodes, ~25 pods in crashloop. 502/504 spike for a subset of requests. Dedicated tenants impacted: MuseAI (prod), internal dev playground. Error rate up ~12% for prod-us-east. attaching quick log excerpt.

mira: ```
[runtime] signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f4a2b0d3f: trt_fused_int8_kernel.cu:421
#0 0x7f4a2b0d3f in trt::fused_int8::execute(...) +0x1f
#1 0x7f4a1e1abc in TRTWrapper::infer(...) +0x3c
#2 0x55a1fbb2 in runtime::Worker::serveLoop() +0x2a0
```

kevin: we shipped TRT-LLM plugin 2.3.4 in the morning deploy. this smells like the int8 fused path regression.

sara: can we keep one pod alive to grab core + backtrace? currently crashloop restarts too fast.

mira: trying to patch the deployment to increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds and disable liveness probe so we can `gcore` a running pid. will also set env `TRT_ENABLE_FUSED_INT8=false` as a quick toggle.

kevin: good call. change image back to 2.3.3 if toggle doesn't stabilize. I can cut the rollback PR.

mira: running commands now: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runtime TRT_ENABLE_FUSED_INT8=false`
mira: `kubectl -n prod patch deploy runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":120,"containers":[{"name":"runtime","livenessProbe":null}]}}}}'`

dan: cordoning the 4 impacted nodes to avoid noisy restarts during mitigation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-07` etc. will schedule replacements on healthy pool.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: rollback image runtime:image-2.3.3 -> runtime/image:2.3.3 @kevin (manual approval required).

kevin: approved and kicking rollback: `kubectl -n prod set image deploy/runtime runtime=registry.redwood/runtime:2.3.3`

mira: able to `kubectl exec` into one pod before it restarts. capturing `gcore` to /var/lib/runtime/cores/core.$(date +%s) and uploading to s3://rw-incidents/4460012345/cores/ .

mira: core and logs uploaded. stacktrace confirms crash inside fused int8 kernel (cuda memcpy near boundary). sending artifact to applied-forensics.

sara: traffic metrics: after env toggle + rolling restart, 502 rate dropped from 12% -> 0.9% across prod-us-east. request latencies returned to normal for MuseAI.

mira: rollback to 2.3.3 completed on all pods in prod cluster. monitoring for 20m.

ops-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied (env toggle + rollback). severity -> P1 -> P0-unstable. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/runbooks/trt-segfault

kevin: root cause looks like a regression in 2.3.4 fused int8 kernel path when input sequence crosses block boundary. we'll open a PR to revert the fused-int8 optimizer until a test is added.

dan: handoff: I'm handing pager to sara for next 8 hrs. any follow-up tasks?

sara: taking handoff. follow-ups: 1) postmortem draft (owner: kevin + mira) 2) add canary for TRT plugin upgrades (owner: eng-platform) 3) add unit/regression test to cover fuse boundary case (owner: eng-ml) 4) add automatic env toggle in deploy pipeline for risky kernel features.

mira: creating incident doc with timeline + artifacts: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4460012345-doc. will include core/backtrace and CI regression that missed this.

kevin: opened PR to disable auto-roll forward in release pipeline for plugin 2.3.x until we have canary gates.

sara: MuseAI support notified; they reported degraded quality earlier but now confirm traffic recovered. flagging for customer success follow-up.

mira: big thumbs to team :thumbsup: will join postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT. marking incident resolved for live mitigation. keeping P0 window until 08:00 UTC for monitoring.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-2026-0913 status -> mitigated (live). Artifacts: s3://rw-incidents/4460012345/ ; assigned postmortem -> kevin, mira.

dan: thanks all. handing off to sara.

sara: got it. logging final note and closing open runbooks.
